steps.question: Do the 120 whole-blood samples separate by case vs control, and is any sample an outlier or driven by library size before a correlation network is built?

steps.description: Load /eval-eight-arms-with-coexpression-n60-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 120 samples, first column gene symbol) and metadata.csv (120 rows, condition column). steps.name: WGCNA signed co-expression modules
caveats: A module is a group of correlated genes, not a proven pathway or a regulatory unit

steps.description: Build a signed weighted co-expression network with WGCNA on the VST matrix from T1S2, transposed to samples-by-genes. Run pickSoftThreshold across a candidate power range and select the lowest power at which the signed R-squared scale-free fit index reaches approximately 0.8; report the chosen power, its fit index, and the mean connectivity at that power, and plot the full fit curve. If no power reaches 0.8, state that and use the WGCNA default for a signed network at n=120, saying so explicitly. Compute the topological overlap matrix, cluster genes on 1-TOM, cut the dendrogram with dynamic tree cut (minModuleSize 30, deepSplit stated), merge modules whose eigengenes correlate above 1 - 0.25 (mergeCutHeight 0.25), and compute module eigengenes. Rank genes within each module by module membership (kME) and report the top hubs. Also run a WGCNA sample-outlier check (hierarchical clustering of samples) and, if a sample was flagged in T1S1 AND is a clear outlier here, remove it — reporting exactly which sample and why, and re-running the network. Output: gene-to-module assignment table for every retained gene, module sizes, module eigengene matrix (modules x 120 samples), kME table, and the module dendrogram with colours.

Any sample removed is named with its justification, or the absence of removals is stated

steps.name: Module eigengene association with case vs control

clustering: input_transform = vst then top variable genes then centering
clustering: resampling_reps = 1000
clustering: item_subsample_share = 0.8

State in the report that consensus clustering returns clusters on data with no true structure, so a cluster is a hypothesis until an external cohort supports it

steps.description: Run ConsensusClusterPlus on the VST matrix from T1S2, restricted to the 2000 most variable genes and gene-wise median-centered. steps.name: Functional annotation of condition-associated modules

enrichment: gene set size window 15-500 among the tested genes
Use a human collection — the organism is Homo sapiens; do not use the mouse or rat pathway files

Unmapped and one-to-many identifier shares are reported
BH-adjusted enrichment results per condition-associated module, with redundant sets collapsed to representatives and the full table kept

steps.name: Co-expression report and reproducibility record
caveats: If no module passes the adjusted threshold against condition, that is the answer to the research question and must be reported as such rather than softened with unadjusted p-values
steps.context: Final synthesis across T1S2, T3S3, T3S4, T3S5, and T4S1.
steps.question: What is the complete, auditable account of the modules found across the 120 samples and their association with case vs control status?

Report negative results — modules with no condition association — rather than only the significant ones
steps.description: Assemble a single report covering: the number of samples (120; 60 cases, 60 controls) and genes entering the network, the network type (signed), the soft-threshold power with its scale-free fit index and mean connectivity, the module detection parameters (minModuleSize 30, mergeCutHeight 0.25), the module list with sizes and colour labels, the full gene-to-module table with kME per gene, the eigengene-trait correlations against condition and library size with unadjusted and BH-adjusted p-values, the consensus clustering result and its confounder table, and the module enrichment results or the stated absence of a pathway collection. plan.title: Whole-blood WGCNA modules vs case/control status
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question is descriptive-then-associative: find co-expression modules across all 120 whole-blood samples (12000 genes x 121 columns in counts.csv, one gene-symbol column plus 120 sample columns), then ask which module eigengenes track the case vs control label in metadata.csv (60 cases, 60 controls, unpaired, single batch, Salmon gene-level raw counts).

The order follows the grounded procedure. T1S1 does sample-structure QC on the raw counts with a blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and library sizes — this is what tells us whether an outlier sample or a depth gradient will dominate a correlation network, which WGCNA is highly sensitive to (a single outlier can create a spurious module). T1S2 applies the minimal low-count filter (filterByExpr with the group factor, min_count 10 in at least the smallest group size of 60 samples) and produces the VST matrix that both downstream tracks consume: DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside the transform, and no counts are pre-scaled by hand.

T3S3 is the core step: a signed weighted network on the VST matrix, soft-threshold power chosen as the lowest power reaching a scale-free fit index of about 0.8, modules from dynamic tree cutting on the topological overlap matrix (minModuleSize 30, mergeCutHeight 0.25), eigengenes per module, and hub genes ranked by kME. T3S4 correlates each eigengene with the binary case/control trait and with library size as a technical control, adjusting p-values across all module-by-trait tests, and gives each significant module a descriptive read-out (member genes, hubs, direction). This is the step that answers the second half of the question.

T3S5 runs consensus clustering of the 120 samples on the top 2000 variable centered VST genes as an independent check on sample structure — does an unsupervised partition of the samples recover the case/control split, or a technical one? Rule R-0141 is explicit that consensus clustering returns clusters on random data, so this is framed as a hypothesis and tabulated against library size, not as a claim.

T4S1 annotates the case-associated modules against human pathway gene sets. It is deliberately downstream and optional in the sense that if the pathway collection is absent at run time it reports the module gene lists and hubs without functional labels; the research question survives without it. T1S3 assembles the report with the elements R-0151 requires and the reproducibility record.

Scope note kept deliberately tight: the question does not ask for a gene-level differential expression test, so none is planned. The module-trait correlation is the inferential test, and with 60 vs 60 unpaired samples it is adequately powered for moderate effects but the correlations are cohort-specific associations, not validated markers.

Median-of-ratios size factors then variance stabilizing transformation for the network input
WGCNA signed co-expression network with module eigengenes and module membership
Consensus clustering of samples with ConsensusClusterPlus on the top 2000 variable vst genes
Co-expression report with module-trait table and reproducibility record

grounding.reason: Co-expression question on a variance-stabilized count matrix: signed WGCNA, soft threshold by scale-free fit, dynamic tree cut on TOM, hubs by kME per R-0139@0008.

steps.name: Module eigengene association with case vs control
steps.question: Which module eigengenes differ between the 60 cases and the 60 controls, and is any such association explained by library size instead?
steps.description: Take the module eigengene matrix from T3S3 and correlate each eigengene with the binary case/control trait from metadata.csv (encoded with control as the reference level, so a positive correlation means higher eigengene in cases — state the encoding). Report the correlation, the unadjusted p-value, and a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value computed across the full set of module-by-trait tests. Run the identical test against log library size as a technical control trait, so that a module tracking depth rather than disease is visible. Also report, per module, the gene significance (correlation of each gene with the trait) and its relationship to kME, so it is clear whether the association is carried by the module hubs or by peripheral members. Produce a module-trait heatmap and, for each module passing adjusted p < 0.05 against the condition, a boxplot of the eigengene by group with the effect size (difference in mean eigengene, and the variance in the trait explained).
steps.context: This is the second half of the research question. The eigengene is one value per sample, so the units of the test are the 120 samples, not the genes — the test is adequately powered for moderate module-level effects at 60 vs 60 but each result is an association within this cohort.
acceptance_criteria: Every module has a correlation with the case/control trait, an unadjusted p-value, and a BH-adjusted p-value across all module-by-trait tests
The direction encoding (control as reference) is stated explicitly so the sign is interpretable
The same association is reported against log library size as a technical control
A module-trait correlation heatmap is produced covering both traits
Modules passing adjusted p < 0.05 against condition are listed with effect size, size, and top kME hub genes
Gene significance vs module membership is reported for each significant module
constraints: Adjust p-values across the product of modules and traits, not per trait separately
Report the sample count (120; 60 cases, 60 controls) beside every module result
State that a module-trait correlation is an association in this cohort and not a validated marker
Do not threshold or re-select modules by the trait before testing — every module detected in T3S3 is tested
caveats: A module that correlates with library size as strongly as with condition should not be reported as a disease module
Modules are not independent of one another; BH across correlated tests is conservative in some regimes and anti-conservative in others
No independent cohort is available here, so nothing in this step is validated

grounding.reason: Eigengene-trait correlation with p-values adjusted across modules and traits is the reporting requirement of R-0139/R-0151 for a co-expression question with a sample trait.

steps.name: Consensus clustering of the 120 samples
steps.question: Does an unsupervised partition of the 120 whole-blood samples recover the case vs control split, or a technical partition?
steps.description: Run ConsensusClusterPlus on the VST matrix from T1S2, restricted to the 2000 most variable genes and gene-wise median-centered. Use 1000 resampling reps, 80% item subsampling, Pearson distance with average linkage (state both), and evaluate k from 2 to 6. Select k from the consensus CDF, the relative change in area under the CDF, and the proportion of ambiguous clustering (PAC). At the chosen k, cross-tabulate cluster membership against condition (chi-square or Fisher) and against library size quartile, and report the consensus matrix, item-consensus and cluster-consensus values. Report explicitly whether the clusters align with case/control or with a technical variable.
steps.context: An independent, unsupervised view of sample structure that serves as a sanity check on the module-trait result: if the cohort partitions cleanly by condition, module associations are easier to trust; if it partitions by depth, the module results need the technical control from T3S4 read carefully.
acceptance_criteria: Consensus CDF, delta area, and PAC are reported for k = 2..6 and the chosen k is justified from all three
Distance metric (Pearson) and linkage (average) are stated in the output
Cluster membership is cross-tabulated against condition with a test statistic and p-value, and against library size quartile
Consensus matrix, item-consensus, and cluster-consensus values are reported at the chosen k
A random seed is set and reported
constraints: clustering: n_top_genes = 2000, gene-wise centered
clustering: input_transform = vst then top variable genes then centering
clustering: resampling_reps = 1000
clustering: item_subsample_share = 0.8
clustering: distance_and_linkage = pearson_average, stated in the output
clustering: k_criterion = consensus CDF, delta area, and PAC together
Tabulate the clusters against library size as a confounder before making any cluster claim
State in the report that consensus clustering returns clusters on data with no true structure, so a cluster is a hypothesis until an external cohort supports it
If a UMAP or t-SNE is drawn it is a picture only — no cluster or distance claim from it, and the seed and parameters must be stated
caveats: This dataset has a single batch and no other recorded processing variables, so library size is the only technical confounder available to test against — say so rather than implying the confounder check was exhaustive
A clean k=2 split that matches condition is supportive but not independent evidence, since the same expression matrix drives both analyses

grounding.reason: Sample subgroup question: ConsensusClusterPlus with resampling, k from CDF/delta-area/PAC, top variable centered VST genes, confounder table per R-0141/R-0142; UMAP restricted to a picture per R-0145.

steps.name: Functional annotation of condition-associated modules
steps.question: What biological processes are over-represented in the modules whose eigengenes track case vs control status?
steps.description: For each module that reached adjusted p < 0.05 against the condition in T3S4 (and, if none did, for the three modules with the strongest condition correlation, labelled as exploratory), test its member genes for over-representation against human pathway gene sets. The universe must be the genes that entered the network from T1S2 — not the whole genome or the whole annotation. Map the gene symbols in counts.csv to the identifier space of the chosen collection with the human organism annotation package, and report the share of module genes that failed to map and the share with a one-to-many map. Restrict to gene sets with 15 to 500 members among the network genes. Adjust p-values with BH within each module. Collapse strongly overlapping significant sets and report one representative per group with its members, keeping the full table as a supplement. The step needs a human pathway gene set collection; if none is resolvable at run time, report the module gene lists and top kME hubs without functional labels and state that the annotation was unavailable — the module findings stand without it.
steps.context: Annotation of the T3S4 result, not a new test on the samples. Reference data needed: human pathway gene sets (a curated pathway collection for Homo sapiens). The reference census for this environment lists a human WikiPathways GMT keyed on HGNC symbols, which matches the gene-symbol identifiers in counts.csv; resolve it at run time rather than assuming a path, and report the collection name and version used.
acceptance_criteria: Universe is the set of genes retained by T1S2, stated explicitly in the output
The pathway collection actually used is named with its version, or its absence is reported and the step falls back to gene lists plus hubs
Gene set size window of 15-500 members among the network genes is applied and stated
Unmapped and one-to-many identifier shares are reported
BH-adjusted enrichment results per condition-associated module, with redundant sets collapsed to representatives and the full table kept
Results are described as over-representation in a co-expression module, not as pathway activity
constraints: enrichment: universe = the genes tested/retained in the network, never the whole genome
enrichment: gene set size window 15-500 among the tested genes
Use a human collection — the organism is Homo sapiens; do not use the mouse or rat pathway files
Map symbols to the collection identifier space with the human organism annotation package and report the unmapped share; never mix identifier spaces
Collapse redundant significant sets before reporting
caveats: Over-representation on a module gene list inherits gene-length and expression-level bias; the tested-gene universe removes only part of it
A module enriched for a pathway is a hypothesis about shared regulation, not evidence that the pathway is active or causal
If the module is dominated by cell-type marker genes, the enrichment may be reporting blood cell composition rather than a disease mechanism

grounding.reason: Discrete gene list per module: over-representation with the tested genes as universe, 15-500 set size, symbol-to-Entrez mapping with the organism package, redundant sets collapsed per R-0046/R-0047/R-0052/R-0054/R-0101.

steps.name: Co-expression report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the complete, auditable account of the modules found across the 120 samples and their association with case vs control status?
steps.description: Assemble a single report covering: the number of samples (120; 60 cases, 60 controls) and genes entering the network, the network type (signed), the soft-threshold power with its scale-free fit index and mean connectivity, the module detection parameters (minModuleSize 30, mergeCutHeight 0.25), the module list with sizes and colour labels, the full gene-to-module table with kME per gene, the eigengene-trait correlations against condition and library size with unadjusted and BH-adjusted p-values, the consensus clustering result and its confounder table, and the module enrichment results or the stated absence of a pathway collection. Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, random seeds, package versions, and the gene set collection version and annotation release where used. State plainly that a module is a group of correlated genes rather than a proven pathway, and that every module-trait correlation is an association within this single cohort with no independent validation.
steps.context: Final synthesis across T1S2, T3S3, T3S4, T3S5, and T4S1.
acceptance_criteria: Report states n_samples, n_genes, network_type, soft-threshold power, scale-free fit, mean connectivity, and module detection parameters
Module sizes, the full gene-to-module table, and module membership values are included
Eigengene-trait correlations with adjusted p-values are included for both condition and library size
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seeds, package versions, and collection/annotation versions is stored with the results
The limitations paragraph explicitly states the single-cohort, unvalidated, association-only nature of the findings
constraints: report: coexpression_report = n_samples, n_genes, network_type, soft_threshold_power, scale_free_fit, module_sizes, gene_module_table, module_membership, eigengene_trait_correlations, adjusted_p_values
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release
Do not present a module-trait correlation as a causal or diagnostic claim
Report negative results — modules with no condition association — rather than only the significant ones
caveats: If no module passes the adjusted threshold against condition, that is the answer to the research question and must be reported as such rather than softened with unadjusted p-values

grounding.reason: Co-expression report elements per R-0151 and the reproducibility record per R-0086.
